name: PenguinComm Speak
desc: The bot's voice: speaks alerts and chat commands out loud with named personas, your wording, limits and quiet hours. Silent until you switch it on.

help.title: VOICE_OPENAI_KEY
help.summary: OpenAI API key. Optional: only needed for cloud voices.
steps: Create an API key in your OpenAI account.
Paste it in Integrations > Key vault as VOICE_OPENAI_KEY with Set, then press Test.
Turn on 'Allow cloud voices' in Speak and set a persona's engine.
The key is never shown, logged or spoken.

help.title: VOICE_ELEVENLABS_KEY
help.summary: ElevenLabs API key. Optional: only needed for cloud voices.
steps: Create an API key in your ElevenLabs account.
Paste it in Integrations > Key vault as VOICE_ELEVENLABS_KEY with Set, then press Test.
Turn on 'Allow cloud voices' in Speak and set a persona's engine.
The key is never shown, logged or spoken.

voice-master.title: Pinguino Voice is switched off
voice-master.summary: This is the normal, safe state: nothing is spoken or played. Previews inside this page still work.
steps: Open the Voice page and pick the persona you like with the Preview buttons (these play inside the page only).
When ready, flip the big master switch to ON. The first test line goes to your normal Windows output.
Use Panic stop any time to silence the queue immediately.

voice-engine.title: Voice engine
voice-engine.summary: The Windows speech engine that turns words into audio.
steps: Needs Windows 10/11 with at least one installed voice (David and Zira come with Windows).
If it fails, open Windows Settings > Time & Language > Speech and add a voice.
Press Test engine on the Voice page; the result shows the voices found.

voice-events.title: Event feed
voice-events.summary: Where follows, subs, raids and cheers come from: the Host's Activity feed.
steps: The Host module must be running (Bots / Host page).
Sign the streamer in on the Host so Twitch events arrive.
Nothing arrives from here when the Host is down; typed !tts and test events still work.

voice-queue.title: Speech queue
voice-queue.summary: Lines waiting to be spoken. Too many waiting means the stream is busy or limits are too loose.
steps: Raise the rate limit and merge similar events in Limits & Queue.
Panic stop empties the queue.

voice-errors.title: Voice engine
voice-errors.summary: The Windows speech engine that turns words into audio.
steps: Needs Windows 10/11 with at least one installed voice (David and Zira come with Windows).
If it fails, open Windows Settings > Time & Language > Speech and add a voice.
Press Test engine on the Voice page; the result shows the voices found.

voice-cloud.title: Cloud voices
voice-cloud.summary: Optional realistic voices from OpenAI or ElevenLabs. Off by default: no text leaves this PC until you allow it.
steps: Open Speak > Personas and set a persona's engine to openai or elevenlabs, with a cloud voice.
Add the key in Integrations > Key vault: VOICE_OPENAI_KEY or VOICE_ELEVENLABS_KEY, then press Test.
Turn on 'Allow cloud voices' in Speak > Limits & queue > Cloud voices.
Only the finished sentence (secrets already removed) is sent. If the cloud fails, the Windows voice speaks instead (can be turned off).

quiet.title: Quiet hours
quiet.summary: Voice is intentionally muted or whispering because of the daily quiet window or a temporary mute.
steps: Change the window in Limits & Queue > Quiet hours.
Press Unmute to cancel a temporary mute.

_module.title: PenguinComm Speak (Pinguino Voice)
_module.summary: The bot's speaking voice (PenguinComm > Speak; Listen is the other half, it hears you). A talking co-host: named voice personas with catchphrases announce follows, subs, raids, cheers and chat commands. Silent unless you switch it on.
steps: Open Voice. The master switch is OFF: nothing is spoken.
Personas tab: tweak a persona (voice, speed, pitch, effects) and press Preview.
Events tab: choose who announces each event and what they say.
Limits & Queue: set profanity, length and rate limits, quiet hours.
Presets: save your whole setup, restore it, share or import one.
Flip the master switch ON when happy. Panic stop silences everything.

voice-output.title: Which voice and where it plays
voice-output.summary: Shows the default persona's voice and the speakers it will use.
steps: Open PenguinComm > Speak > Limits & queue > Output and pick the device (empty = Windows default speakers).
Press Sound check in the page header: you should hear one line.
If the device says 'not found', it is unplugged or renamed: pick it again.
Keep the bot voice OFF your microphone: use headphones or a separate output so Listen does not hear it.

voice-loop.title: Bot voice and the microphone
voice-loop.summary: Listen hears whatever your mic hears. If the bot speaks through speakers next to the mic, Listen transcribes the bot.
steps: Best: play the bot on headphones or on a different output device than your monitors (Speak > Limits & queue > Output).
Speak publishes when it is talking: GET :8772/api/speech-intervals and the file Data\runtime\voice\speaking.json, so Listen can ignore those moments.
Voice commands are never answered in chat, so a loop cannot trigger bot replies; it can only add bot lines to the transcript.
